title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. S is a regular connected scheme of finite type over Q. k is the algebraic closure of Q in Γ(S,O_S), so k/Q is finite and S is geometrically connected over k. An embedding σ: k→C is fixed.

Motives. M is a Q-linear tensor category of smooth, 'iso' (isogeny-type), semisimple motives over S, and it is of finite type (tensor-generated by one object). The embedding σ determines one isomorphism class of Q-valued fibre functors on M: the Betti realizations T_ξ: M ↦ H_B(M_ξ), for ξ ∈ S(C) above σ. They are all isomorphic because the Betti realizations form local systems on the connected space S(C)_σ. Fix one such T and put G = Aut⊗(T). This is an algebraic group over Q, the motivic Galois group of M, and M ≅ Rep_Q(G) by Tannaka duality.

The torsor P. Define P = Isom⊗(T_S, T_DR), where T_S = T⊗O_S is the constant fibre functor and T_DR sends M to its de Rham realization, a vector bundle on S. P is a right G_S-torsor on S. Two structures come with it:
- An integrable connection relative to k (equivalently relative to Q, since k/Q is finite étale), compatible with the G_S-action. This is the Gauss–Manin connection, packaged as a connection on a principal bundle.
- A ⊗-filtration on T_DR ≅ (M ↦ P ×^{G_S} M_S) on Rep(G). This is the Hodge filtration, i.e. a filtered fibre functor.
In modern terms, P is the relative (family) version of the period torsor Isom⊗(ω_B, ω_dR) carrying the Gauss–Manin connection and Hodge filtration.

Analytic side. Over C there is a covering P̄_C → S(C) whose fibre at ξ is Isom⊗(T, T_ξ). It is a principal covering with discrete group G(Q). The text writes S̄_C here, a slip. The Betti–de Rham comparison gives a map p: P̄_C → P^an_C which is G(Q)-equivariant and horizontal for the connections. So P̄_C is a reduction of the structure group of the flat bundle P^an from G(C) to G(Q), coming from the rational monodromy.

Crossed-out start, redone on the next page. A period map f: P̄_C → 𝒱_G, the space of Hodge structures on G_R (homomorphisms S → G_R compatible with a fixed weight cocharacter G_m → G), with three conditions:
- (a) f is holomorphic;
- (b) f(xg) = g^{-1} f(x) for g ∈ G(Q);
- (c) a compatibility with the Hodge filtration, presumably Griffiths transversality.

What it serves. The previous page uses this formalism to show (modulo the Hodge conjecture) that P/R descends to k as a torsor, where R is the algebraic monodromy group. This amounts to a 'theorem of the fixed part' / monodromy-normality statement for motivic Galois groups in families. The overall programme is to describe a family of motives over S by group-theoretic data: G, the monodromy representation π_1 → G(Q), a G-torsor with connection and filtration, and a period map into a Mumford–Tate-type domain.
errors: Slip: 'S̄_C est un revêtement principal de S(C), de groupe G(Q)' should be P̄_C. The universal cover S̄_C only enters on the next page.

Implicit hypotheses: the isomorphism class of fibre functors depends on the connected component S(C)_σ, which is fine because S/k is geometrically connected and σ is fixed. Whether T_DR is a ⊗-functor valued in locally free O_S-modules, with the filtration exact (a filtered fibre functor), is assumed rather than proved, as is the full faithfulness needed for M ≅ Rep(G). All of this is conjectural ('standard conjectures'-dependent) in 1965.
The period map conditions are only begun here and crossed out; condition (c) (transversality) is not stated on this page.

ideas.what: Motivic Galois group G = Aut⊗(T) of a finitely generated category of motives over a base S, with M ≅ Rep(G)
ideas.modern_name: Tannakian motivic Galois group (relative/over a base)
ideas.where_published: Only via Récoltes et Semailles mentions and Saavedra's thesis; not in EGA/SGA

ideas.what: P = Isom⊗(T_B⊗O_S, T_DR), a G_S-torsor with integrable (Gauss–Manin) connection and Hodge ⊗-filtration
ideas.modern_name: Period torsor in families / torsor of periods with Gauss–Manin connection; filtered flat G-bundle
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Hodge cycles on abelian varieties, 1982), Kontsevich–Zagier 2001, André (1992, 2004), Ayoub/Nori relative period torsors
ideas.where_published: unsure; the period conjecture is only alluded to in Lang's 1966 transcendental numbers book

ideas.what: Reduction of the flat analytic G(C)-bundle to a principal G(Q)-covering P̄_C via Betti fibre functors at varying points, with horizontal equivariant comparison p
ideas.modern_name: Rational monodromy representation π_1 → G(Q) attached to a variation of motives

ideas.what: Period map from the G(Q)-covering into the space of Hodge structures on G_R (homomorphisms S→G_R with a fixed weight), holomorphic and equivariant (crossed out here, developed on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Period map into a Mumford–Tate domain G(R)/M; group-theoretic VHS (Shimura-datum-like)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Griffiths (period domains, 1968–70), Deligne (Travaux de Shimura 1971, 1979), Green–Griffiths–Kerr (Mumford–Tate domains, 2012)

missed.claim: A 1965 formulation of the relative period torsor Isom⊗(T_S, T_DR) as a G_S-torsor with Gauss–Manin connection and Hodge ⊗-filtration, followed by a period map into the space of Hodge structures on G_R. This is essentially the Tannakian/Mumford–Tate-domain description of variations of motives, predating Griffiths' period domains in this group-theoretic form and Deligne's Tannakian period torsor.
missed.quote: P = Isom⊗(T_S, T_DR) est un torseur sous G_S. Il est muni d'une connexion intégrable relativement à k ... compatible avec G_S. De plus le foncteur T_DR ... est muni d'une ⊗-filtration
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority point. The structure (G-torsor + connection + filtration + rational monodromy reduction + period map to a G(R)-homogeneous domain) is what André, Deligne and Green–Griffiths–Kerr later use. It shows Grothendieck had the 'motivic' version of Mumford–Tate domains and the fixed-part/monodromy argument (previous page) in 1965. It is not a new mathematical result for specialists today.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly setup, but setup of a notable kind: it is an explicit 1965 Tannakian period torsor in families with Gauss–Manin connection and Hodge filtration, plus a G(Q)-equivariant period map into a space of Hodge structures on G_R. These are standard now (Deligne, André, GGK) but are not credited to Grothendieck in this form. There is no new theorem on this page itself.
transcription_corrections: 'S̄_C est un revêtement principal' is what is written, but it is a slip for P̄_C.
The crossed-out line after 'Soit' reads roughly 'G un foncteur fibre de cette classe, et G un groupe alg./Q (évident) isomorphe aux Hom_k(Spec C, S)' — the 'Hom_k(Spec C,S)' reading is uncertain.
'{+rel/Q+}' above 'fibres' is an insertion meaning 'fibre functors relative to Q' (Q-valued).
